permutationDefect.summary: Every learner's first uninterrupted attempt was graded against options other than the ones they clicked.
mechanism: The form is fetched before an attempt exists, so getCurrentAssessment served options in AUTHORED order (activeAttemptId undefined).
Pressing Start created attempt N. The learner page does not refetch the form, so it kept showing authored order.
The page records the clicked DISPLAYED index.
submitAssessment re-derived getAttemptQuestionPermutation(N, ...) and graded permutation[clicked] against the key - a permutation the learner never saw.
additionalDefects: isDiagnosticAnswerCorrect compared a displayed index directly with the authored correctIndex when the permutation was missing, and also when permutation[answer] was undefined because the index was out of range (fail open).
submitAssessment without attemptId created a NEW COMPLETED attempt graded with no permutation, bypassing the no-retake rule and orphaning the in-progress attempt.
toResult guessed the permutation with 'attempt.id >= 50', so an attempt created by that path was displayed with a different grade from the one stored.
toResult called weightedCore(questions, answers, attempt.id), a sixth attempt-seeded grading path not listed in earlier audits.
A client-supplied { originalIndex } was accepted as the authored option identity.

correction.permutationSeed: getLearnerQuestionPermutation(userId, assessmentId, questionId, optionCount). userId is the authenticated JWT subject; no client value enters the seed. The served order is therefore identical before Start, after Start, on resume and on review, so the page's existing behaviour becomes correct without a frontend change.
correction.grader: resolveAuthoredOptionIndex returns the authored index or null. A displayed index needs a VALID permutation of exactly the option count and an in-range integer; otherwise null. Option text resolves only when exactly one option matches. originalIndex is refused. isDiagnosticAnswerCorrect = resolved !== null && resolved === correctIndex.
correction.attemptAuthority: submitAssessment requires attemptId, loads the attempt, requires the caller's userId and this assessmentId, returns the recorded result for a COMPLETED attempt without regrading, rejects any status other than IN_PROGRESS, and never creates an attempt.
correction.serialization: a pg_advisory_xact_lock on the attempt id plus a status re-read under the lock, so a racing duplicate returns the completed attempt instead of grading and rewarding twice.
correction.failClosedBeforeWrite: every objective answer must resolve through the server permutation before the transaction opens.
correction.persistedScheme: answers.__permScheme = LEARNER_ASSESSMENT_V1. toResult re-derives the permutation from that scheme; an attempt stored by the old code with __permAttemptId is re-derived with its own scheme; an attempt with neither yields unresolvable index answers rather than a guess.
